description: Synthetic generic software-engineering retrieval fixture. Forty documents form twenty precise near-neighbor pairs; labels are frozen before model evaluation.

documents.text: SQL transaction isolation: use READ COMMITTED when each statement may see newly committed rows and short blocking is preferred.
SQL transaction isolation: use REPEATABLE READ when all statements in one transaction must observe a stable snapshot.
HTTP retries: retry idempotent GET and PUT requests with exponential backoff and jitter after transient 5xx responses.
HTTP retries: do not automatically retry non-idempotent POST requests unless the API provides an idempotency key.
Cache policy: set a finite TTL so entries expire and stale values are eventually refreshed.
Cache invalidation: actively evict affected keys after a successful write when immediate freshness is required.
Queue delivery: at-least-once consumers must acknowledge only after durable processing completes.
Queue delivery: exactly-once business effects require a deduplication key or idempotent handler even with acknowledgements.
Logging security: redact passwords, access tokens, and authorization headers before writing logs.
Logging operations: preserve a request correlation ID so events from one request can be traced across services.
Unicode input: normalize user identifiers to NFC before equality checks to unify canonically equivalent sequences.
Unicode input: apply case folding only when the field's semantics define case-insensitive matching; preserve original display text.
Filesystem security: reject paths whose normalized form escapes the designated root directory to prevent traversal.
Filesystem behavior: resolve symbolic links according to policy before access checks because a link can escape the apparent root.
React hooks: include every render-dependent value in a useEffect dependency array to avoid stale closures.
React hooks: use a functional state updater when a callback derives next state from the previous value.
Graceful shutdown: stop accepting new work, drain in-flight requests, then close resources before the deadline.
Graceful shutdown: enforce a hard termination timeout after which remaining work is cancelled and the process exits.
Database migrations: expand-contract begins by adding backward-compatible columns or tables before switching writers.
Database migrations: contract removes obsolete columns only after all readers and writers no longer depend on them.
API pagination: cursor tokens represent a stable position and avoid duplicates when rows are inserted during traversal.
API pagination: offset pagination is simple for static collections but can skip or repeat rows under concurrent writes.
Distributed locks: renew a lease before expiry and attach an ownership token to prevent an old holder from releasing a new lock.
Distributed locks: a mutex in one process coordinates local threads but provides no cross-process exclusion.
Metrics: counters record monotonically increasing occurrences such as requests or errors.
Metrics: gauges represent values that rise and fall, such as queue depth or active connections.
Python async code: await the coroutine returned by an async function or it will not execute to completion.
Python async errors: RuntimeWarning: coroutine was never awaited indicates a coroutine object was dropped without await or task scheduling.
TLS validation: verify the server certificate chain and hostname; disabling verification is unsafe for production traffic.
TLS client authentication: mutual TLS additionally requires the client to present a certificate accepted by the server.
JSON schema evolution: adding an optional field with a default is backward compatible for readers that ignore unknown fields.
JSON schema evolution: renaming or removing a required field is breaking until all producers and consumers migrate.
Container health: liveness checks should answer whether the process should be restarted, not whether every dependency is healthy.
Container health: readiness checks should fail when the instance must be removed from traffic, such as a database outage.
Security headers: Content-Security-Policy restricts which scripts and resources a browser may load.
Security headers: Strict-Transport-Security tells browsers to use HTTPS for a host during a defined max-age.
Go maps: concurrent read and write access without synchronization can trigger fatal error: concurrent map read and map write.
Go slices: append may reallocate backing storage, so retaining pointers or aliases requires understanding capacity and ownership.
Search ranking: BM25 scores term frequency and document length for lexical relevance.
Search ranking: vector cosine similarity compares embedding direction to retrieve semantically related wording.
